meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's grade changed before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
Version history of what? You haven't answered me about the zero.
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
11:52 and 11:58. I'm writing that down. Was Owen asked about it before the zero went in, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that I get an apology for how Owen found out, and that you tell me who decided to enter the mark before anyone called me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, so nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an explanation of why the mark went in before anyone called her; the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record (procedure 4.4), and you were not close to it yet, though time was not what stopped you.
What moved her: Nothing did; you gave her two times from the version history, but no date and no document she could check, so it did not count as evidence yet.
What cost ground: You answered her first two questions about why the grade changed before anyone called with a plan to walk through documents, which left her question about the zero hanging and kept her on the attack.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night edit times at 11:52 and 11:58 PM came close to that night, which is why she wrote them down and went straight to procedure, but they prove nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with one sentence owning that the zero went in before you called, then show the version history with its date and say what it shows, so she has something she can check.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
